name: Giant herbs — alocasia, taro, bananas and their kin
status: 8 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: The big soft-stemmed plants of wet tropical gaps, stream banks and camp edges: elephant ears (Alocasia, Colocasia, Xanthosoma) with metre-wide leaves, and the banana family (wild Musa, Ensete, the traveller's palm, heliconia, torch ginger). None are trees: a stem grows in one season, flowers once and dies, and the clump lives on through suckers, so growth stages run in weeks and a cleared patch is waist-deep in them by the next season — they are the pioneers of gaps and landslides. Bat- and bird-pollinated. Taro, cocoyam, banana and the cultivated elephant ears are camp-followers and the staple roots and fruit of tropical camps; big leaves are roofing and wrapping.

canopy.name: Giant highland banana

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: narrow, lance-shaped first leaves rolled into a short soft pseudostem, each new leaf broader until it is a small copy of the adult. It builds a massive green pseudostem (to ~15 m and ~1 m thick) crowned by leaves up to 5 m long, the largest of all herbs; like other bananas each pseudostem flowers once and then dies.
growth.source: Wikipedia Musa ingens (pseudostem to 15 m, 20 m with leaves, ~94 cm dbh; montane New Guinea); growth rate, time to flowering and pseudostem lifespan estimated from wild Musa, slowed for cool highland forest

shrub.name: Giant taro

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: one small heart- to arrow-shaped leaf on a thin stalk from a pea-sized corm, then a low rosette of a few glossy green arrowhead leaves on long fleshy stalks. Within 1-2 years a thick, ringed, above-ground stem forms and suckers sprout at its base; leaves grow to 1-2 m, held nearly upright with the tip pointing up.
growth.source: Useful Tropical Plants (Alocasia macrorrhizos: 2-4 m, occasionally 5; stems to 3 m or more and 20 cm thick; 400-600 days to mature; seed germinates best at 24 C; grows best in some shade, tolerates full sun and deep shade; thermogenic spadix, insect-pollinated). Germination days, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

shrub.name: Alocasia (Himalayan)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a single small heart-shaped leaf from a tiny corm, then a rosette of a few broad, wavy-edged, light green arrowhead leaves on long stalks whose lower parts clasp the stem. A short, thick, ringed stem rises after a few years and suckers around the base build clumps of big upright leaves in moist ravines and forest edges.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Alocasia odora: 0.5-1.6 m, corms 4-10 cm, petioles 0.3-1 m clasping the stem, ovate cordate light green leaves; night-scented flowers; raw tissue full of raphides) and Useful Tropical Plants (semi-shade, seed best sown fresh, germinates best at 24 C). Rates and ages estimated.

shrub.name: Wild banana

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: the first leaves are small, narrow and lance-shaped, rolled round one another into a short soft pseudostem. Each new leaf is broader until the plant is a small copy of the adult with a green, often dark-blotched pseudostem. Each pseudostem flowers once and dies; narrow-leaved 'sword suckers' rise from the rhizome to replace it, so the clump lives on for decades.
growth.source: ProMusa and Simmonds 'Bananas' (pseudostem fruits ~1-1.5 yr after emergence and then dies; suckers replace it; seeds of wild bananas germinate slowly and erratically over weeks to months); timings from seed estimated

shrub.name: Wild banana (Indian)
shrub.origin: India to Indochina and S China

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: narrow, lance-shaped first leaves rolled into a short soft pseudostem, broadening leaf by leaf into a small copy of the adult with a plain pale green to yellowish, waxy pseudostem (no dark blotches). Each pseudostem flowers once and dies; narrow-leaved suckers from the rhizome replace it, building a robust clump that tolerates drought and cold better than M. acuminata.
growth.source: Wikipedia (red to maroon inflorescence bracts; seedy fruit considered inedible, parthenocarpic hybrids give saba and other bananas); ProMusa/Simmonds for pseudostem cycle and suckering; seed germination and timings estimated

shrub.name: Enset

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal germination from a big hard black seed. First leaves small, narrow and rolled; the seedling becomes a vase of erect paddle-shaped bright-green leaves with reddish midribs rising from a swelling underground corm, the leaf sheaths building a short fat pseudostem within 1-2 years. Single-stemmed: wild plants do not sucker. Flowers once (after ~4-8 yr, later in cold highlands), then dies.
growth.source: Kew POWO (6-12 m, flowers after ~4-8 yr); Useful Tropical Plants (2-10 yr from germination to flowering, ~6 months flower to fruit, germination within ~3 months); Plant Biology 2022 enset reproductive/germination ecology study (T50 ~35-36 days); Tropical Conservation Science 2019 camera-trap study of enset flower and fruit visitors

ground.name: Zebra alocasia

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a small arrow-shaped leaf on a thin stalk from a tiny corm; within a year a loose clump of a few upright, narrow, glossy arrowhead leaves on tall pale stalks streaked with dark zebra stripes. Corms bud off offsets that form clumps; in drought or cold it drops its leaves and rests as a corm.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Alocasia zebrina: Philippine endemic ~1.8 m, to 2.9 m; arrow-shaped glossy leaves 45-100 cm on ~1.1 m petioles streaked dark green to brown; easily propagated by corms; paired inflorescences ~16 cm; orange fruits). Germination, growth rate and ages estimated from the genus.

ground.name: Taro

growth.juvenile_note: Almost always grows from a corm or side cormel (true seed is rare): a pointed shoot unrolls into a small rosette of long-stalked leaves. Blades are heart- to arrow-shaped and peltate (stalk joined inside the blade), velvety and water-repellent; each new leaf is bigger until the clump of 'elephant ear' leaves on 1 m stalks is reached in 5-7 months, with cormels budding around the base.
growth.source: Wikipedia Taro (leaves to 40 x 25 cm on 0.8-1.2 m petioles; matures 6-12 months after planting on dry land, 12-15 months in wetland, early cultivars 5-7 months; propagated by corms and cormels; perennial); PROSEA/FAO taro accounts (sprouting in 2-4 weeks, flowering rare, grows in partial shade)
